purpose: Machine-readable chronology of major IsoGraph and Project Discovery ideas, formulations, mission changes, and contribution boundaries. Entries state earliest evidence currently located; they are not global priority determinations.

entries.title: Agent-oriented compact reasoning representation / context-logic incubation

conversation_evidence.summary: Stated that the language was for agents, emphasizing context-window compactness and synthesis of concepts.

reasoning_path: Complex reasoning can exceed available context/working-state capacity even when local operations are tractable.
A compact state should preserve propositions, dependencies, scopes, alternatives, provenance, and inference obligations.
History may be quotiented only when valid future continuations remain unchanged.
The first public Axiomesh record therefore framed a search for a token-efficient, recoverable logical/structural state for agents.
entries.notes: The seed README explicitly says 'Research direction: Josh Oshiro'. 'Josh Oshiro' is the historical short-form name for Joshua Oshiro.

entries.title: Graph/hypergraph rewrite substrate and structure-plus-transformation formulation

attribution.detail: Adopted the proposal as a candidate research direction and continued directing its development.

earliest_evidence.summary: Assistant proposed graph/hypergraph rewriting as a candidate substrate and the formulation of knowledge as structure plus lawful transformation.

reasoning_path: The initial Markov-like sufficient-state idea had to preserve nonlocal dependencies, guards, quantifiers, alternatives, and provenance.
The design pressure favored a sparse typed relational structure over a simple chain.
Graph/hypergraph rewriting unified represented state and lawful transformation while supporting composition, self-representation, isomorphism, and residual accounting.
entries.notes: This record deliberately does not attribute the graph/hypergraph-rewrite proposal or the compact structure-plus-transformation wording solely to Joshua Oshiro.

entries.title: One semantic structure / no mandatory internal translation boundary
reasoning_path: A translator between a source formalism and a separate agent formalism would confound representation, decomposition, mapping, and translation loss.
The project therefore made the structural form both semantic representation and native wire representation, with human/theorem-prover/database views downstream.
entries.notes: The surviving evidence establishes the design under Joshua's research direction but does not support clean sole-origin attribution for this exact formulation.

entries.title: Observation-first discrepancy handling: error/defect may be a clue

conversation_evidence.summary: Stated that a discrepancy might be a clue to look deeper rather than something to normalize away immediately.
Accepted and reinforced an observation-first posture: anomalies should be understood before judging or repairing them.
Strengthened the rule: discrepancies/errors should be preserved and investigated as possible clues; even the expected/reference authority may be wrong.
Clarified that concrete examples normally express a general principle, not a request for a special-case rule.

reasoning_path: Unexpected mismatch may indicate a bug, hidden distinction, hidden equivalence, wrong reference expectation, scope mismatch, or unresolved structure.
Therefore preserve the observation before assigning defect ownership.
When repair is justified, use it as a diagnostic intervention and see what disappears or survives.
Keep repair disposition separate from discovery disposition.

entries.result_summary: The original 12-dimensional cap is imposed. One-line uncapped Chromium control reached 120 dimensions at step 2500; a separately transcribed local Node control reached 143 at step 3000. Every recorded dimension birth followed the explicit cooldown plus self-created edge-length error. Spring-off leaves dimension births but removes projected multi-revolution circulation. Coordinate separation and source mechanics strongly influence visible circulation.

entries.title: Genuinely higher-order branching hypergraph sweep and matched overlapping-relation feedback controls

attribution.contribution: Recalled previous random graph-rewrite × node sweeps, requested a bounded repetition, identified combinatorial rule search as the main difficulty, and insisted on genuinely higher-order interactions rather than pairwise approximations.

Defined a finite permutation-symmetric family of rank3/4/5 atomic hyperedge branching operations and two distinct follow-up controls (coupled node-state mutation; pairwise-projection information loss).

Executed 5,760 fixed-rank finite rewrite trials, 640 coupled-rank trials, 1,440 matched mutable/fixed-state pairs (2,880 runs), 168 relabel tests and exact irreducibility controls; preserved negative results and censoring.

entries.earliest_evidence_currently_located: 2026-10-12 Causal Step conversation: user asks to rerun random graph-rewrite/node-condition steady-state search, elaborates 3/4/5 participant rule combinatorics and explicitly disallows pairing-only models; precise excerpts in research/causal-step/DISCUSSION_LOG.md.
entries.findings: Exact code-level rank3/4/5 hyperedge existence cannot be reconstructed from only its complete pairwise projection. Fixed-state sweeps show no nontrivial stationary global state; 1,534 activated fixed-rank runs that absorbed stopped after precisely one rewrite. Mixed rank 3→4→5 firing was demonstrated in 80/640 runs. In 1,440 matched mutable vs fixed-state pairs, 134 mutable runs reactivated old overlapping hyperedges (0 fixed-state), with 97 pairs changing absorb/horizon outcome. Additional 1,024 rank3/4/5 rewrite trials over 64 matched ruleset/node-bit choices and eight different five-node initial hyperedge patterns each (two schedulers): 50 of 64 rulesets changed absorbing/continuing outcome across initial incidence patterns, with no resource-limit stops.
entries.limits: Results concern a selected finite rule representation, arbitrary binary node-state rewriting and host observation horizons with no physical model or empirically validated particle emergence. Every productive rewrite monotonically adds a node, forbidding exact full-state cycles. One finite sample cannot establish a universal/unbounded hypergraph theorem. No historical frozen source or qualified semantic authority was amended. The initial higher-order configuration sweep sampled eight of 65,536 labeled five-node incidence masks and did not exhaust the rule×initial-hypergraph space.

researcher_noncollapse_correction.verbatim: I feel like you misunderstood what I meant by steady state. I meant a state that does not collapse. It can grow forever. We just need to see it not collapse.
researcher_noncollapse_correction.content: Previous assistant demand for exact global recurrence/fixed point was too strong and is not the researcher's intended criterion. Noncollapse includes indefinite branching and may include halted-but-persistent structure; finite horizon survival and absorbing state are distinct, neither equivalent to structural collapse.

entries.later_mathematical_result: Inductive proof: in the unlimited-resource fixed-k uniform-bit subfamily, an enabled homogeneous hyperedge rewrites into k newly enabled same-rank hyperedges, maintaining F(t)=1+(k-1)t>0. This yields at least 64/256/1024 perpetual rule settings for k3/k4/k5 among the symmetric restricted family, with 59 certified settings in the prior 192-per-k sample. This is a built-in sufficient rule condition rather than an emergent physical process; because node deletion is absent and every fired edge has >=1 higher-order replacement, all runs are predisposed to topological nonemptiness.

entries.findings: 864 exploratory trajectories: 280 initially inert; 231 stopped rewriting after activity; 237 remained productive with simple periodic local tails; 44 remained productive with provisional sustained diverse feedback; 72 unresolved. 432/432 baseline single-edge cases matched prior dynamics in selected diagnostics. At 400 rewrites, 12/14 mutated cases retained provisional feedback complexity screen and 0/14 fixed-state controls did; alternate scheduler seed preserved candidate counts. One complete k5 rule plus same FIFO scheduler exhibited simple and more varied activity under different initial node-bit states.
entries.limits: These are selected, finite k-ary toy models with aggregate binary states and deliberately supplied state mutation; initial rule sampling is enriched, thresholds post-hoc, signatures not graph-isomorphism invariants, no proof of algorithmic complexity/universality/particle structure, and no model of natural physical space/time. Trivial forever-branching witness may coexist with other global structural behavior and is not a rule-wide impossibility proof.

long_horizon_followup.findings: A total of 53 finite longer-run replay trajectories were actually executed, totaling 284,000 simulated rewrite events: 28 at 3,000, 18 at 8,000 and seven different scheduler-seed 8,000 runs. All remained active without resource censoring. The original source's 400-rewrite results matched 448/448 tested fields exactly. Of 14 state-mutating primary contexts, 11 passed the exploratory local complexity screen at 3,000 and 12 at 8,000; the seven alternate scheduler-seed random versions also passed. k5 rule81 FIFO retained exact period5 local behavior despite ongoing growth and reactivation. k4 rule21 FIFO had only two recent local event types and remained unresolved; five other rule-context combinations passed under both schedulers.
long_horizon_followup.boundaries: An observed finite-horizon local event trace is not a proof of computation universality, graph-invariant organized complexity, indefinite survival, particle emergence, or physical law. The model guarantees one node per productive rewrite. The local feedback/period criteria were selected after prior exploration.
